sanskrit: sa rāmapreṣitaḥ kṣipraṃ saṃtāpakaluṣendriyaḥ praviśya nṛpatiṃ sūto niḥśvasantaṃ dadarśa ha
english: Sent swiftly by Rāma, his senses clouded with grief, the charioteer entered and found the king sighing deeply.

sanskrit: ālokya tu mahāprājñaḥ paramākula cetasaṃ rāmam evānuśocantaṃ sūtaḥ prāñjalir āsadat
english: Seeing the king's mind utterly distraught and lamenting for Rāma alone, the greatly wise charioteer sat down with folded hands.

sanskrit: ayaṃ sa puruṣavyāghra dvāri tiṣṭhati te sutaḥ brāhmaṇebhyo dhanaṃ dattvā sarvaṃ caivopajīvinām
english: "This son of yours, tiger among men, stands at the door, having distributed wealth to the brāhmaṇas and to all who depend upon him."

sanskrit: sa tvā paśyatu bhadraṃ te rāmaḥ satyaparākramaḥ sarvān suhṛda āpṛcchya tvām idānīṃ didṛkṣate
english: "May Rāma of true valor see you — may it be well with you; having taken leave of all his friends, he now desires to behold you."

sanskrit: gamiṣyati mahāraṇyaṃ taṃ paśya jagatīpate vṛtaṃ rājaguṇaiḥ sarvair ādityam iva raśmibhiḥ
english: "He is about to depart for the great forest — behold him, O lord of the earth, encircled by all the qualities of a king, as the sun is encircled by its rays."

sanskrit: sa satyavādī dharmātmā gāmbhīryāt sāgaropamaḥ ākāśa iva niṣpaṅko narendraḥ pratyuvāca tam
english: That king — truthful, righteous in soul, deep as the ocean, spotless as the sky — answered him.

sanskrit: sumantrānaya me dārān ye ke cid iha māmakāḥ dāraiḥ parivṛtaḥ sarvair draṣṭum icchāmi rāghavam
english: "Sumantra, bring me all my wives who are here; surrounded by all my consorts I wish to behold Rāghava."

sanskrit: so 'ntaḥpuram atītyaiva striyas tā vākyam abravīt āryo hvayati vo rājā gamyatāṃ tatra māciram
english: Passing into the inner apartments, he spoke to those women: "The noble king summons you — go there without delay."

sanskrit: evam uktāḥ striyaḥ sarvāḥ sumantreṇa nṛpājñayā pracakramus tad bhavanaṃ bhartur ājñāya śāsanam
english: Thus addressed by Sumantra on the king's command, all the women set out for that dwelling, heeding their lord's decree.

sanskrit: ardhasaptaśatās tās tu pramadās tāmralocanāḥ kausalyāṃ parivāryātha śanair jagmur dhṛtavratāḥ
english: Those seven hundred and fifty women of copper-red eyes, firm in their vows, surrounding Kausalyā, moved forward slowly.

sanskrit: āgateṣu ca dāreṣu samavekṣya mahīpatiḥ uvāca rājā taṃ sūtaṃ sumantrānaya me sutam
english: When his wives had arrived, the lord of the earth surveyed them and said to the charioteer: "Sumantra, bring me my son."

sanskrit: sa sūto rāmam ādāya lakṣmaṇaṃ maithilīṃ tadā jagāmābhimukhas tūrṇaṃ sakāśaṃ jagatīpateḥ
english: The charioteer then swiftly led Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, and Maithilī before the lord of the earth.

sanskrit: sa rājā putram āyāntaṃ dṛṣṭvā dūrāt kṛtāñjalim utpapātāsanāt tūrṇam ārtaḥ strījanasaṃvṛtaḥ
english: The king, seeing his son approaching from afar with joined hands, leapt swiftly from his seat in anguish, surrounded by the women.

sanskrit: so 'bhidudrāva vegena rāmaṃ dṛṣṭvā viśāṃ patiḥ tam asaṃprāpya duḥkhārtaḥ papāta bhuvi mūrchitaḥ
english: The lord of the people rushed toward Rāma with speed; before he could reach him, stricken with sorrow, he fell to the ground in a swoon.

sanskrit: taṃ rāmo 'bhyapātat kṣipraṃ lakṣmaṇaś ca mahārathaḥ visaṃjñam iva duḥkhena saśokaṃ nṛpatiṃ tadā
english: Rāma rushed quickly to him, and so did the great warrior Lakṣmaṇa — to the king who lay as though senseless, overwhelmed with grief.

sanskrit: strīsahasraninādaś ca saṃjajñe rājaveśmani hāhā rāmeti sahasā bhūṣaṇadhvanimūrchitaḥ
english: A wail arose from a thousand women throughout the royal palace — the cry "Alas, Rāma!" suddenly overwhelmed by the clamor of their ornaments.

sanskrit: taṃ pariṣvajya bāhubhyāṃ tāv ubhau rāmalakṣmaṇau paryaṅke sītayā sārdhaṃ rudantaḥ samaveśayan
english: Both Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa embraced him with their arms and, weeping, laid him together with Sītā upon his couch.

sanskrit: atha rāmo muhūrtena labdhasaṃjñaṃ mahīpatim uvāca prāñjalir bhūtvā śokārṇavapariplutam
english: Then, after a moment, when the lord of the earth had regained consciousness — inundated in an ocean of grief — Rāma spoke to him with joined hands.

sanskrit: āpṛcche tvāṃ mahārāja sarveṣām īśvaro 'si naḥ prasthitaṃ daṇḍakāraṇyaṃ paśya tvaṃ kuśalena mām
english: "I take leave of you, great king — you are the lord of us all; behold me, who am about to depart for the Daṇḍaka forest, and send me off with your blessing."

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇaṃ cānujānīhi sītā cānveti māṃ vanam kāraṇair bahubhis tathyair vāryamāṇau na cecchataḥ
english: "Grant leave also to Lakṣmaṇa, and to Sītā who follows me into the forest — though dissuaded with many true reasons, neither of them is willing to desist."

sanskrit: anujānīhi sarvān naḥ śokam utsṛjya mānada lakṣmaṇaṃ māṃ ca sītāṃ ca prajāpatir iva prajāḥ
english: "Grant leave to all of us — Lakṣmaṇa, Sītā, and me — setting aside your grief, O giver of honor, as Prajāpati gives leave to his creatures."

sanskrit: pratīkṣamāṇam avyagram anujñāṃ jagatīpateḥ uvāca rarjā saṃprekṣya vanavāsāya rāghavam
english: As Rāghava waited patiently for the leave-granting of the lord of the earth, the king gazed upon him and spoke of the forest-dwelling.

sanskrit: ahaṃ rāghava kaikeyyā varadānena mohitaḥ ayodhyāyās tvam evādya bhava rājā nigṛhya mām
english: "I, O Rāghava, have been deluded by the boon-gift of Kaikeyī; restrain me now and yourself become king of Ayodhyā this very day."

sanskrit: evam ukto nṛpatinā rāmo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ pratyuvācāñjaliṃ kṛtvā pitaraṃ vākyakovidaḥ
english: Thus addressed by the king, Rāma — best among upholders of dharma, skilled in speech — replied to his father with joined hands.

sanskrit: bhavān varṣasahasrāya pṛthivyā nṛpate patiḥ ahaṃ tv araṇye vatsyāmi na me kāryaṃ tvayānṛtam
english: "You are lord of the earth for a thousand years, O king; I shall dwell in the forest. No falsehood need be done by you on my account."

sanskrit: śreyase vṛddhaye tāta punarāgamanāya ca gacchasvāriṣṭam avyagraḥ panthānam akutobhayam
english: "For your welfare and prosperity, dear father, and for my return hereafter — go in peace, undisturbed, by a path free from all danger."

sanskrit: adya tv idānīṃ rajanīṃ putra mā gaccha sarvathā mātaraṃ māṃ ca saṃpaśyan vasemām adya śarvarīm tarpitaḥ sarvakāmais tvaṃ śvaḥkāle sādhayiṣyasi
english: "But do not go this very night at all, my son; seeing your mother and me, spend this night here; gratified in all your desires, you may set out at dawn."

sanskrit: atha rāmas tathā śrutvā pitur ārtasya bhāṣitam lakṣmaṇena saha bhrātrā dīno vacanam abravīt
english: Then Rāma, having heard thus the words of his grief-stricken father, spoke sorrowfully to his brother Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: prāpsyāmi yān adya guṇān ko me śvastān pradāsyati apakramaṇam evātaḥ sarvakāmair ahaṃ vṛṇe
english: "Whatever merits I may acquire today, who will grant me those same ones tomorrow? Therefore I choose departure itself over all pleasures."

sanskrit: iyaṃ sarāṣṭrā sajanā dhanadhānyasamākulā mayā visṛṣṭā vasudhā bharatāya pradīyatām
english: "Let this earth — with its kingdoms, its people, abundant in wealth and grain, relinquished by me — be given over to Bharata."

sanskrit: apagacchatu te duḥkhaṃ mā bhūr bāṣpapariplutaḥ na hi kṣubhyati durdharṣaḥ samudraḥ saritāṃ patiḥ
english: "Let your grief depart; do not be overwhelmed with tears; for the invincible ocean, lord of rivers, is not disturbed."

sanskrit: naivāhaṃ rājyam icchāmi na sukhaṃ na ca maithilīm tvām ahaṃ satyam icchāmi nānṛtaṃ puruṣarṣabha
english: "I desire neither kingship, nor comfort, nor even Maithilī — I desire only your truth, not untruth, O bull among men."

sanskrit: puraṃ ca rāṣṭraṃ ca mahī ca kevalā mayā nisṛṣṭā bharatāya dīyatām ahaṃ nideśaṃ bhavato 'nupālayan vanaṃ gamiṣyāmi cirāya sevitum
english: "The city, the kingdom, and the whole earth — relinquished by me — let them be given to Bharata; I, honoring your command, shall go to the forest to serve it for a long time."

sanskrit: mayā nisṛṣṭāṃ bharato mahīm imāṃ saśailakhaṇḍāṃ sapurāṃ sakānanām śivāṃ susīmām anuśāstu kevalaṃ tvayā yad uktaṃ nṛpate yathāstu tat
english: "Let Bharata govern this earth — relinquished by me — with its mountain ranges, its cities, and its forests, auspicious and well-bounded; only let what you have said, O king, stand as it is."

sanskrit: na me tathā pārthiva dhīyate mano mahatsu kāmeṣu na cātmanaḥ priye yathā nideśe tava śiṣṭasaṃmate vyapaitu duḥkhaṃ tava matkṛte 'nagha
english: "My mind is not so fixed on great pleasures, O king, nor even on what is dear to myself, as it is on fulfilling your command approved by the righteous — let your sorrow on my account depart, O sinless one."

sanskrit: tad adya naivānagha rājyam avyayaṃ na sarvakāmān na sukhaṃ na maithilīm na jīvitaṃ tvām anṛtena yojayan vṛṇīya satyaṃ vratam astu te tathā
english: "Therefore today I would choose neither the imperishable kingdom, nor all pleasures, nor comfort, nor Maithilī, nor even life itself, so as to involve you in falsehood — let your vow of truth remain so."

sanskrit: phalāni mūlāni ca bhakṣayan vane girīṃś ca paśyan saritaḥ sarāṃsi ca vanaṃ praviśyaiva vicitrapādapaṃ sukhī bhaviṣyāmi tavāstu nirvṛtiḥ
english: "Eating fruits and roots in the forest, beholding mountains, rivers, and lakes, entering the forest with its manifold trees, I shall be content — may you find peace."

sanskrit: tataḥ sumantram aikṣvākaḥ pīḍito 'tra pratijñayā sabāṣpam atiniḥśvasya jagādedaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
english: Then the scion of Ikṣvāku, tormented by this pledge, breathing in deep sighs with tears, spoke again and again.

sanskrit: sūta ratnasusaṃpūrṇā caturvidhabalā camūḥ rāgavasyānuyātrārthaṃ kṣipraṃ pratividhīyatām
english: "Charioteer, let an army of the fourfold force, richly furnished with gems, be swiftly prepared to escort Rāghava."

sanskrit: rūpājīvā ca śālinyo vaṇijaś ca mahādhanāḥ śobhayantu kumārasya vāhinīṃ suprasāritāḥ
english: "Let graceful courtesans of excellence, and merchants of great wealth, spread out and adorn the prince's retinue."

sanskrit: ye cainam upajīvanti ramate yaiś ca vīryataḥ teṣāṃ bahuvidhaṃ dattvā tān apy atra niyojaya
english: "Those who depend upon him and those with whom he delights to display his valor — assign them here too, after giving them manifold gifts."

sanskrit: nighnan mṛgān kuñjarāṃś ca pibaṃś cāraṇyakaṃ madhu nadīś ca vividhāḥ paśyan na rājyaṃ saṃsmariṣyati
english: "Hunting deer and elephants, drinking the wild honey of the forest, beholding the various rivers, he will not remember the kingdom."

sanskrit: dhānyakośaś ca yaḥ kaś cid dhanakośaś ca māmakaḥ tau rāmam anugacchetāṃ vasantaṃ nirjane vane
english: "Whatever treasury of grain and treasury of wealth I possess — let both follow Rāma as he dwells in the desolate forest."

sanskrit: yajan puṇyeṣu deśeṣu visṛjaṃś cāptadakṣiṇāḥ ṛṣibhiś ca samāgamya pravatsyati sukhaṃ vane
english: "Performing sacrifices at sacred places, distributing gifts with fitting fees, and meeting with sages, he will dwell happily in the forest."

sanskrit: bharataś ca mahābāhur ayodhyāṃ pālayiṣyati sarvakāmaiḥ punaḥ śrīmān rāmaḥ saṃsādhyatām iti
english: "Long-armed Bharata shall protect Ayodhyā; may glorious Rāma be fully provided with all that he desires and then return."

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvati kākutsthe kaikeyyā bhayam āgatam mukhaṃ cāpy agamāc choṣaṃ svaraś cāpi nyarudhyata
english: As the scion of Kākutstha spoke thus, fear came upon Kaikeyī; her face grew parched and her voice choked.

sanskrit: sā viṣaṇṇā ca saṃtrastā kaikeyī vākyam abravīt rājyaṃ gatajanaṃ sādho pītamaṇḍāṃ surām iva nirāsvādyatamaṃ śūnyaṃ bharato nābhipatsyate
english: Dejected and fearful, Kaikeyī spoke: "O virtuous one, a kingdom emptied of its people, like wine from which the cream has been drunk, utterly tasteless and barren — Bharata will not accept such."

sanskrit: kaikeyyāṃ muktalajjāyāṃ vadantyām atidāruṇam rājā daśaratho vākyam uvācāyatalocanām vahantaṃ kiṃ tudasi māṃ niyujya dhuri māhite
english: When Kaikeyī spoke thus, utterly shameless, in the most cruel manner, King Daśaratha said to her of the wide eyes: "Why do you torment me, harnessing me to a yoke not fit to bear?"

sanskrit: kaikeyī dviguṇaṃ kruddhā rājānam idam abravīt tavaiva vaṃśe sagaro jyeṣṭhaṃ putram upārudhat asamañja iti khyātaṃ tathāyaṃ gantum arhati
english: Kaikeyī, doubly enraged, said this to the king: "In your own lineage, Sagara obstructed his eldest son — known as Asamañja — and so this one also deserves to go."

sanskrit: evam ukto dhig ity eva rājā daśaratho 'bravīt vrīḍitaś ca janaḥ sarvaḥ sā ca tan nāvabudhyata
english: Thus addressed, King Daśaratha only exclaimed "Shame!" and all the assembled people were mortified — but she took no heed of this.

sanskrit: tatra vṛddho mahāmātraḥ siddhārtho nāma nāmataḥ śucir bahumato rājñaḥ kaikeyīm idam abravīt
english: There an aged chief minister, Siddhārtha by name, pure in conduct and highly regarded by the king, said this to Kaikeyī.

sanskrit: asamañjo gṛhītvā tu krīḍitaḥ pathi dārakān sarayvāḥ prakṣipann apsu ramate tena durmatiḥ
english: "Asamañja, seizing children to play with along the path and flinging them into the waters of the Sarayū — this wicked-minded one amused himself thus."

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā nāgaraḥ sarve kruddhā rājānam abruvan asamañjaṃ vṛṣīṇvaikam asmān vā rāṣṭravardhana
english: "Seeing this, all the citizens, enraged, said to the king: choose between Asamañja alone and us, O increaser of the realm."

sanskrit: tān uvāca tato rājā kiṃnimittam idaṃ bhayam tāś cāpi rājñā saṃpṛṣṭā vākyaṃ prakṛtayo 'bruvan
english: "The king then said to them: what is the cause of this fear? And the subjects, questioned by the king, spoke their grievance."

sanskrit: krīḍitas tv eṣa naḥ putrān bālān udbhrāntacetanaḥ sarayvāṃ prakṣipan maurkhyād atulāṃ prītim aśnute
english: "'This one, out of his senses, snatches our young children to play with and out of folly casts them into the Sarayū, enjoying incomparable delight.'"

sanskrit: sa tāsāṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā prakṛtīnāṃ narādhipa taṃ tatyājāhitaṃ putraṃ tāsāṃ priyacikīrṣayā
english: "Hearing the words of his subjects, O lord of men, Sagara abandoned that harmful son, wishing to do what was dear to them."

sanskrit: ity evam atyajad rājā sagaro vai sudhārmikaḥ rāmaḥ kim akarot pāpaṃ yenaivam uparudhyate
english: "Thus the most righteous king Sagara indeed abandoned his son. What sin has Rāma committed, that he should be obstructed in this manner?"

sanskrit: śrutvā tu siddhārthavaco rājā śrāntatarasvanaḥ śokopahatayā vācā kaikeyīm idam abravīt
english: Hearing the words of Siddhārtha, the king — his voice still more exhausted — spoke thus to Kaikeyī in a voice afflicted by grief.

sanskrit: anuvrajiṣyāmy aham adya rāmaṃ rājyaṃ parityajya sukhaṃ dhanaṃ ca sahaiva rājñā bharatena ca tvaṃ yathā sukhaṃ bhuṅkṣva cirāya rājyam
english: "I shall follow Rāma today, abandoning the kingdom, comfort, and wealth; together with King Bharata, enjoy the kingdom at leisure for a long time as you please."

sanskrit: mahāmātravacaḥ śrutvā rāmo daśarathaṃ tadā anvabhāṣata vākyaṃ tu vinayajño vinītavat
english: Having heard the words of the minister, Rāma then addressed Daśaratha, versed in courtesy, speaking in a courteous manner.

sanskrit: tyaktabhogasya me rājan vane vanyena jīvataḥ kiṃ kāryam anuyātreṇa tyaktasaṅgasya sarvataḥ
english: "For me who have renounced enjoyments, O king, living in the forest on forest fare, who have relinquished all attachments — what need is there of an escort?"

sanskrit: yo hi dattvā dvipaśreṣṭhaṃ kakṣyāyāṃ kurute manaḥ rajjusnehena kiṃ tasya tyajataḥ kuñjarottamam
english: "For one who has given away the finest elephant and then sets his mind upon the halter-rope — what use is that rope's attachment to one who has relinquished the finest elephant?"

sanskrit: tathā mama satāṃ śreṣṭha kiṃ dhvajinyā jagatpate sarvāṇy evānujānāmi cīrāṇy evānayantu me
english: "So for me likewise, O best among the righteous, O lord of the earth — what use is an army? I renounce everything; let only bark-cloth garments be brought for me."

sanskrit: khanitrapiṭake cobhe mamānayata gacchataḥ caturdaśa vane vāsaṃ varṣāṇi vasato mama
english: "Bring also a spade and a basket for me as I depart; I shall dwell in the forest for fourteen years."

sanskrit: atha cīrāṇi kaikeyī svayam āhṛtya rāghavam uvāca paridhatsveti janaughe nirapatrapā
english: Then Kaikeyī herself fetched bark-cloth garments and, shamelessly, before the multitude, said to Rāghava: "Put these on."

sanskrit: sa cīre puruṣavyāghraḥ kaikeyyāḥ pratigṛhya te sūkṣmavastram avakṣipya munivastrāṇy avasta ha
english: That tiger among men accepted the bark-cloth from Kaikeyī, laid aside his fine garment, and put on the ascetic's dress.

sanskrit: lakṣmaṇaś cāpi tatraiva vihāya vasane śubhe tāpasāc chādane caiva jagrāha pitur agrataḥ
english: Lakṣmaṇa too, right there, setting aside his auspicious garments, took on the hermit's covering before his father.

sanskrit: athātmaparidhānārthaṃ sītā kauśeyavāsinī samīkṣya cīraṃ saṃtrastā pṛṣatī vāgurām iva
english: Then Sītā — clad in silk — gazed at the bark-cloth meant for her own wearing, trembling like a doe caught in a snare.

sanskrit: sā vyapatrapamāṇeva pratigṛhya ca durmanāḥ gandharvarājapratimaṃ bhartāram idam abravīt kathaṃ nu cīraṃ badhnanti munayo vanavāsinaḥ
english: Receiving it as if with shame, downcast in heart, she said to her husband — who was like the king of gandharvas: "How do the sages who dwell in the forest tie the bark-cloth?"

sanskrit: kṛtvā kaṇṭhe ca sā cīram ekam ādāya pāṇinā tasthau hy akuṣalā tatra vrīḍitā janakātmaja
english: She, the daughter of Janaka, unskilled in this and ashamed, draped one strip of bark-cloth around her neck and held another in her hand, and stood there not knowing how to proceed.

sanskrit: tasyās tat kṣipram āgamya rāmo dharmabhṛtāṃ varaḥ cīraṃ babandha sītāyāḥ kauśeyasyopari svayam
english: Coming quickly to her, Rāma — best among upholders of dharma — himself tied the bark-cloth over Sītā's silk garment.

sanskrit: tasyāṃ cīraṃ vasānāyāṃ nāthavatyām anāthavat pracukrośa janaḥ sarvo dhik tvāṃ daśarathaṃ tv iti
english: As she who had a protector was being dressed in bark-cloth as if she had none, all the people cried out: "Shame upon you, Daśaratha!"

sanskrit: sa niḥśvasyoṣṇam aikṣvākas tāṃ bhāryām idam abravīt kaikeyi kuśacīreṇa na sītā gantum arhati
english: Sighing a hot breath, the scion of Ikṣvāku said to that wife: "Kaikeyī, Sītā does not deserve to go clad in kusa-bark."

sanskrit: nanu paryāptam etat te pāpe rāmavivāsanam kim ebhiḥ kṛpaṇair bhūyaḥ pātakair api te kṛtaiḥ
english: "Is not the banishment of Rāma itself enough of a sin for you, wicked woman? What need of these further wretched transgressions committed by you?"

sanskrit: evaṃ bruvantaṃ pitaraṃ rāmaḥ saṃprasthito vanam avākśirasam āsīnam idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Even as his father spoke thus, Rāma — already setting out for the forest — spoke these words to him who sat with his head bowed down.

sanskrit: iyaṃ dhārmika kausalyā mama mātā yaśasvinī vṛddhā cākṣudraśīlā ca na ca tvāṃ devagarhite
english: "This Kausalyā — righteous, illustrious, my mother, aged and of noble character — let her not be held in contempt by you in an act censured by the gods."

sanskrit: mayā vihīnāṃ varada prapannāṃ śokasāgaram adṛṣṭapūrvavyasanāṃ bhūyaḥ saṃmantum arhasi
english: "O giver of boons, you must take thought once more for her — bereft of me, plunged into an ocean of grief, facing a misfortune such as she has never known before."

sanskrit: imāṃ mahendropamajātagarbhiṇīṃ tathā vidhātuṃ janamīṃ mamārhasi yathā vanasthe mayi śokakarśitā na jīvitaṃ nyasya yamakṣayaṃ vrajet
english: "You must so provide for this my mother — who bore within her a child comparable to great Indra — that, wasting away in grief while I abide in the forest, she does not lay down her life and depart to the realm of Yama."
